title: Season Planning, Hardening-Off and Transplant Timing

content.overview: Outdoor establishment requires matching plant readiness with local weather. Frost risk, day length, cultivar growth habit, root development and transplant conditioning all influence whether plants establish quickly or lose time to stress.

vocabulary.definition: Gradual acclimation of protected young plants to stronger outdoor light, wind and temperature variation.
Temporary stress and growth reduction after a plant is moved into a new root and atmospheric environment.
The part of the local season between expected damaging frosts.

sections.title: Local climate defines the planting window
sections.body: Outdoor planting should follow local frost risk and field conditions rather than a universal calendar date. Production system and cultivar type also affect how much season length is needed.

sections.title: Protected plants need acclimation
sections.body: Plants started indoors or under greenhouse conditions may encounter stronger sunlight, greater wind and wider temperature swings outdoors. A gradual transition reduces abrupt stress.

sections.title: Root readiness matters
sections.body: A transplant should have enough root development to maintain water balance after planting without being excessively root-bound. Soil moisture at transplant and follow-up irrigation are part of establishment planning.

workedExamples: Warm afternoons do not eliminate the risk of a damaging cold night; use local forecast and frost history rather than one warm day.
Seedlings raised under gentle indoor light may need several staged exposures before full outdoor sun.
commonMistakes: Moving tender plants directly into full wind and sun.
Planting from a fixed holiday date without checking local weather.
content.practicalApplication: Record expected frost dates, cultivar type, target transplant window and acclimation steps. Increase outdoor exposure progressively and transplant when both plant condition and field conditions are suitable.
content.summary: Successful outdoor establishment aligns plant readiness with weather and season. Hardening-off, root condition and local frost risk are more useful than a one-date-fits-all planting rule.
